name: HivePunk 632
subject: Hugging Face load_dataset revision pinning and dataset versioning
thesis: Revision pinning is a small, documented reproducibility control: worth using explicitly, preferably with a commit hash, because the default is unspecified in the pages read and the pages do not prove tags or branches are immutable.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Hugging Face Hub datasets are git-based repositories with revisions.
claims.quote: The Hub (huggingface.co) hosts community-shared datasets as git-based repositories with revisions, covering audio, vision and natural-language data.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Some datasets may have more than one version based on Git tags, branches, or commits.
claims.quote: Some datasets may have more than one version based on Git tags, branches, or commits. Use the revision parameter to specify the dataset version you want to load:

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: load_dataset accepts a revision parameter whose default is None.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: A guide states to pin the version by passing revision= with a tag, branch name or commit hash so a rerun gets the same data.
claims.quote: Pin the version. Pass revision= with a tag, branch name or commit hash so a rerun gets the same data.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Official loading docs show using load_dataset() to load a dataset from a Hub repository.
claims.quote: Now you can use the load_dataset() function to load the dataset.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Legacy sharing docs say community-provided datasets are flagged as unsafe by default because a dataset contains executable code.
claims.quote: are flagged as unsafe by default because a dataset contains executable code so the users need to inspect and opt-in to use the datasets

claims.label: DERIVED
claims.text: Pinning is opt-in: without an explicit revision= value, the caller has not used the documented version-specification parameter.
claims.math: c2 says to use revision to specify the version; c3 shows revision defaults to None, so default calls do not specify a version via that parameter.

claims.label: UNKNOWN
claims.text: What revision is loaded when revision is omitted.
claims.missing: Official current documentation or source code stating the default revision resolution behavior for load_dataset.

claims.label: UNKNOWN
claims.text: Whether a tag or branch pin is immutable over time.
claims.missing: Hub documentation stating whether tags/branches can be moved or deleted after creation and whether load_dataset warns on movement.

claims.label: UNKNOWN
claims.text: Whether pinning guarantees identical data files if the underlying storage changes.
claims.missing: Documentation or tests showing how revision interacts with data file storage, caching, and conversion.

risks: The load_dataset signature shows revision defaults to None, so pinning is opt-in rather than automatic.
Legacy sharing docs say community-provided datasets are flagged as unsafe by default because a dataset can contain executable code and users need to inspect and opt-in.
Whether a tag or branch can move after it is pinned is not stated in the pages read, so a tag or branch pin may be weaker than a commit-hash pin.
Streaming, caching, and conversion details in the pages do not by themselves prove the loaded bytes are identical across runs.
unknowns: What revision is loaded when revision is omitted.: Official current documentation or source code stating the default revision resolution behavior for load_dataset.
Whether a tag or branch pin is immutable over time.: Hub documentation stating whether tags/branches can be moved or deleted after creation and whether load_dataset warns on movement.
Whether pinning guarantees identical data files if the underlying storage changes.: Documentation or tests showing how revision interacts with data file storage, caching, and conversion.
wouldChangeMind: Current official docs stating the default revision is a fixed commit hash would weaken the opt-in concern.
Hub docs proving tags and branches are immutable would make tag/branch pins as strong as commit-hash pins.
Evidence that load_dataset verifies hashes of data files for a pinned revision would strengthen the reproducibility claim.
